body:
Closes #40458

## Problem

`nvim.dir` hard-codes filesystem listing and navigation, so other bundled directory-like browsers cannot reuse its listing UI.

## Solution

Move filesystem-specific operations behind a small, private `nvim.dir.Provider` interface. `nvim.dir` renders provider entries and installs buffer-local mappings and reload handling, while listing state remains owned by the buffer instead of a parallel registry.

| Surface | Role |
| --- | --- |
| `nvim.dir.open(buf, name, provider)` | Open `buf` as a listing named `name` using `provider`. |
| `Provider.list_entries(buf, name, cb)` | Produce entries or report an error. |
| `Provider.open_entry(buf, name, entry)` | Open the entry under the cursor. |
| `Provider.open_parent(buf, name)` | Open the parent listing. |
| `Provider.attach(buf, name)` | Perform optional provider-specific buffer setup after a successful open. |

The filesystem implementation uses this interface without persistent provider state. The global `-` mapping continues to open the parent filesystem directory.

comment_data.body:
i don't get why we need this. just put the state on the buffer.

the "provider" system should not turn into some big "manager" or "registry".

a basic `Provider` shape is fine, just for interface purposes. but there should be no registry/manager.

+function load(buf, name, provider, restore_view, setup)
+  local list_generation = vim._assert_integer(vim.b[buf].nvim_dir_generation or 0) + 1

+  -- Used to abort failed first opens while preserving the old listing on reload failure.
